profile.facility_type_note: Part of QTS's Atlanta-area campus, spanning Atlanta proper, Fayette County, and Gwinnett County, Georgia. Georgia (Atlanta) was one of QTS's earliest markets, per Wikipedia's account of the company's 2005-2007 acquisition-driven expansion.

reading.body:
The QTS Atlanta campus occupies 99 acres across four buildings with a combined critical power capacity of 278 MW. This is the fifth-largest published capacity in Georgia, where only 4 facilities among 33 mapped data centers disclose their power specifications. The Atlanta campus represents 4.2% of Georgia's 66.3 MW of published critical power capacity.

A 278 MW campus supports roughly 6,950 racks at typical AI training density of 40 kW per rack, or approximately 2,300 GPU clusters of 3-rack configurations. Whether the campus meets AI-grade specifications for cooling architecture, power redundancy, or networking density is not published.

QTS Atlanta was established during the company's early expansion phase in 2005-2007, long before modern AI infrastructure requirements solidified. The facility's current qualification for contemporary AI workloads depends on infrastructure details the operator has not disclosed in public specifications.
